To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) multitasking while reading text on a computer screen is detrimental to reading efficiency, (2) reading text on paper or a computer screen is equally efficient, and (3) the presence of the Internet and a printer on a computer screen reduces the quality of a report written based on reading text, but the use of paper for active reading and note-taking reduces the negative effects of the presence of the internet and a printer.
(a) reading on paper and reading on a screen are equally good for reading comprehension and (b) reading on a screen is better than reading on paper for writing quality.
reading on a screen is not significantly different from reading on paper for either reading comprehension or for writing a synthesis report.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of screen reading and multitasking conditions on reading and writing among college students.
the impact of reading and writing on electronic screens and with the impact of multitasking while reading on learning outcomes.
the impact of screen reading and multitasking conditions on reading and writing, among college students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reading from screens, especially with multitasking, has no impact on reading comprehension.

paper and screens have similar impact on reading comprehension, but reading on a screen without Internet and printer access may be more beneficial for writing, especially if note-taking on paper is allowed.
the use of paper for reading and writing in college classrooms may be beneficial, but the benefits are not always as large as we might expect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
paper and screen conditions were not different in terms of reading comprehension and writing performance, but the opportunity to multitask had a negative impact on efficiency.
reading on a computer screen is not inherently worse than reading on paper, and that multitasking can have a detrimental impact on reading comprehension.
the medium and multitasking conditions had a greater impact on writing than reading, and that the medium had a greater impact than multitasking on writing, but not on reading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the real-world, students should be encouraged to read source texts on computer screens and to use paper for taking notes, rather than reading source texts on paper.
reading and writing on paper and screens are similar, but reading and writing on screens can be made more effective by limiting distractions.
the medium of the text is not the most important factor for learning.
